input: Hello, ma'am. What is the reason for your visit today? I was referred by a doctor to come see you so that you could check up on my nasal problems. Here is my report from my previous doctor who referred me to you. Thank you. Let me take a look. I see here it says you had severe sinusitis two to three months ago, correct? Is that what they're calling my nasal problems? Yeah, it is. Sinusitis is the inflammation of your nasal airways. I see. Thank you for describing it to me. No problem. Would you be able to describe to me what you had been feeling two to three months ago? Yeah, I can. My face would feel uncomfortable, my nose was stuffy, my eyes hurt, and I felt something dropping in the back of my throat. Have you ever been prescribed any medication? Here's the list of medicine I was taking. I see you were given antibiotics, correct? I was, but I don't know what those are. Could you explain them to me? Antibiotics are usually used to fight infections. I had an infection? I thought I just had some nasal problems. Your report states you had a severe infection. Do you remember if the antibiotics helped? Not really. I felt like my symptoms were the same. I see. Did your doctor order any advanced imaging's? Yeah. They did a C T scan of my nose. Here is the report from my C T scan. Let me take a look. It looks like you had some thickening of the mucosal layer in your right paranasal sinus. You also had some obstruction in your right ostiomeatal complex and excess growing of some of the bones in your nose. Uhm. Oh, one more thing. I see your nasal septum was shifted to the left. Oh, wow. Thank you for explaining everything to me. No problem. Going back to your list of medications, I know you took antibiotics for your infection, but did you take any medication for your sinuses? No, I haven't. I did try this cream for my nose, but that didn't work either. Nothing worked! I see. Looks like the cream you used was a topical nasal corticosteroid. Are there any other symptoms that you have been experiencing? I've had some trouble with my balance, and I feel like I've lost some of my hearing. I thought this was odd since I'm only fifty years old. I think my ears felt plugged or full of air, so they just needed to pop. I see. Let's perform an audiogram test to check your ears. Sounds good. I'm seeing that you have some mild high frequency sensorineural hearing loss. Your tympanometry seems to be normal. Your speech discrimination was also normal. That's reassuring. I want to ask a few more questions about your ears. Do you feel any fullness or pressure? No, I don't feel anything like that right now. Do you hear any humming, buzzing, or roaring sounds? Nope. I don't hear anything like that. We checked your ears and now understand more about the problem, but I wonder why your balance is affected. When did you start noticing your balance was affected? I think it could have been to this one medicine that starts with an A. I forgot the name, but it didn't really help my nasal problems. It just made my balance worse. Was the medicine called Allegra? Oh, yeah. That's what it was called. I thought I had some sort of allergy, so I thought it would help. I see. Did you ever feel any dizziness too? Yeah, I did. I will have you do some movements to see if your dizziness occurs. Sounds good. Could you look to the left and then look to the right. Oh, wow. That made me very dizzy. Looks like sudden movements and head turning make your dizziness worse.

Subjective:

- Severity: severe sinusitis reported two to three months ago; mild high frequency sensorineural hearing loss noted.
- Duration: symptoms of sinusitis experienced two to three months ago; balance issues and hearing loss currently ongoing.
- Associated symptoms: dizziness with sudden movements and head turning.
- Relevant medical history: previous diagnosis of severe sinusitis, prescribed antibiotics, CT scan showing thickening of mucosal layer, obstruction in right ostiomeatal complex, and a shifted nasal septum.
- Family history: not mentioned.
- Allergies: medication (Allegra) caused worsening balance; no other allergies mentioned.
- Concerns: frustration with previous treatments (antibiotics and topical nasal corticosteroid) not being effective; anxiety regarding balance issues and hearing loss at age 50.

Objective:
- CT scan findings: thickening of the mucosal layer in the right paranasal sinus, obstruction in the right ostiomeatal complex, excess growth of some bones in the nose, shifted nasal septum.
- Audiogram results: mild high frequency sensorineural hearing loss, normal tympanometry, normal speech discrimination.

Assessment:
- Diagnoses: chronic sinusitis with a history of severe acute exacerbation, mild high frequency sensorineural hearing loss, possible medication-induced dizziness related to Allegra.

Plan:
- Perform an audiogram test to monitor hearing.
- Evaluate and possibly adjust current medications to address nasal problems and balance issues.
- Further investigate the cause of dizziness related to sudden movements.
- Educate the patient on the findings and management options for their nasal and ear symptoms.
